'''Jerzy Andrzej Filar''' (born August 30, 1949, in [[Warsaw]], Żoliborz) is an Australian mathematician of Polish origin, His interests include [[operations research]], [[Stochastic modeling|stochastic modelling]], [[game theory]], [[Markov decision process]]es, [[Perturbation theory|perturbation]] [[theory]], and [[environmental modelling]].<ref name="EmerJAF">{{Cite web |date=2025-01-23 |title=Emeritus Professor Jerzy Filar |url=https://smp.uq.edu.au/profile/330/jerzy-filar |access-date=2025-01-24 |website=smp.uq.edu.au |language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
He received his early education at Primary School No. 1 in [[Warsaw]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=wikom.pl |first=Wikom |title=Historia |url=https://jedynka.edu.pl/strona/historia |access-date=2025-01-24 |website=Szkola Podstawowa nr 1 |language=pl-PL}}</ref>  In 1964, he moved to [[Melbourne]], [[Australia]], where he attended [[Kew High School]]. In 1972, he obtained a B.Sc (Hons) degree in [[Mathematical statistics|Mathematical Statistics]] from the [[University of Melbourne Faculty of Science|University of Melbourne]], followed by an M.Sc. in [[Statistics education|Statistics]] from [[Monash University]] in 1975, and a M.A. in [[Mathematics]] from [[University of Illinois Chicago]] in 1977.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Professor Jerzy Filar |url=https://www.flinders.edu.au/people/jerzy.filar |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=Flinders University |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":5">The documents concerning education are in the private archive of Filar's family</ref> In 1980, he completed his PhD at the University of Illinois Chicago, defending his thesis titled ''Algorithms for Solving Undiscounted Stochastic Games''.<ref name="JAFMGP">{{Cite web |title=Jerzy Filar – The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=6730 |access-date=2025-01-24 |website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu |archive-date=2024-12-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241203175910/https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=6730 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Filar |first=Jerzy Andrzej |title=Algorithms for solving some undiscounted stochastic games – ProQuest |url=http://gateway.proquest.com/openurl?url_ver=Z39.88-2004&rft_val_fmt=info:ofi/fmt:kev:mtx:dissertation&res_dat=xri:pqdiss&rft_dat=xri:pqdiss:8014224 |access-date=2025-01-24 |website=www.proquest.com |language=en}}</ref> His doctoral advisor was [[T. E. S. Raghavan|T.E.S. Raghavan]].<ref name="TRagMGP">{{Cite web |title=Thirukkannamangai Raghavan – The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=38650 |access-date=2025-01-24 |website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Filar |first=Jerzy A. |date=2023-12-01 |title=Flinders University – Adelaide, South Australia |url=https://www.flinders.edu.au/people/jerzy.filar |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250320062318/https://www.flinders.edu.au/people/jerzy.filar |archive-date=2025-03-20 |access-date=2025-04-14 |website=Flinders University |language=en |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Since 1975, Jerzy A. Filar held various academic positions at institutions across [[Australia]] and the United States. He began his career as a Tutor at [[Monash University]] (1975–1976) before serving as a Visiting assistant professor at the [[University of Minnesota]] (1979–1980). He then held faculty positions at [[Johns Hopkins University]] (1980–1986) and the [[University of Maryland, Baltimore County]] (1986–1991), where he progressed from Associate to Full Professor.<ref name=":5" />

In 1992, he joined [[University of South Australia]] as Professor of Mathematics and Statistics, later serving as Director of the Centre for Industrial and Applied Mathematics (1994–1998) and Foundation Chair of Mathematics and Statistics (2001–2011). He then became Strategic Professor at [[Flinders University]] (2011–2016)<ref name=":0" /> and later Professor of Applied Mathematics and Director of the Centre for Applied Resource Mathematics at the [[University of Queensland]] (2016–2020).<ref name="EmerJAF" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=CARM research group |url=https://smp.uq.edu.au/taxonomy/term/294 |access-date=2025-02-10 |website=smp.uq.edu.au |language=en |archive-date=2025-02-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250203173232/https://smp.uq.edu.au/taxonomy/term/294 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=CARM |title=Centre for Applications in Natural Resource Mathematics (CARM) |url=https://smp.uq.edu.au/files/15608/CARM }}</ref>

Filar also served as a supervisor or co-supervisor in over thirty Ph.D. dissertations.<ref name="JAFMGP" />

Filar retired at the end of 2020 and assumed the role of emeritus Professor at the [[University of Queensland]].<ref name="EmerJAF" />

== Research impacts ==
Filar is an [[applied mathematician]] with research interests in [[operations research]], [[Modeling and simulation|stochastic modelling]], [[Mathematical optimization|optimization]], [[game theory]], and [[environmental modelling]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Filar |first=Jerzy Andrzej |date=2025-02-02 |title=Publication in selected journals (Web of Science) |url=https://www.webofscience.com/wos/author/record/B-3824-2019 |access-date=2025-01-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Filar |first=Jerzy Andrzej |title=ORCID |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5587-2541 |access-date=2025-01-25 |website=orcid.org}}</ref> He supervised or co-supervised 31 PhD theses.{{r|JAFMGP}}{{r|EmerJAF}}

He authored 148 scholarly works, including articles, books, book chapters, and conference papers.<ref name="JAFzbl">{{cite web |last=Filar |first=Jerzy A. |date=1976 |title=Publication reviewed in zbMATH |url=https://zbmath.org/authors/filar.jerzy-a |access-date=2021-02-19 |website=zbMATH Open |language=en |number=FIZ Karlsruhe GmbH}}<!-- auto-translated from Polish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref name="MathSciNet">{{cite web |last=Filar |first=Jerzy Andrzej |date=1976 |title=List of publication in MathSciNet |url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/search/author.html?mrauthid=66790 |access-date=2021-02-19 |website=MathSciNet |language=en |number=American Mathematical Society}}<!-- auto-translated from Polish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Filar |first=Jerzy A. |date=2025-02-02 |title=Publication in indexed journals (SCOPUS) |url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=7005332085&origin=resultslist }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jerzy Filar – University of Queensland – AD Scientific Index 202 – 2025 |url=https://www.adscientificindex.com/scientist/jerzy-filar/114909 |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=www.adscientificindex.com}}</ref> Three books are:

* ''Competitive Markov Decision Processes'' (Springer, 1997; co-authored with K. Vrieze) serves as a textbook on [[stochastic game]]s and [[Markov decision process]]es, under the unifying concept of "[[Competition|Competitive]] [[Markov decision process]]es" for [[Discrete-time dynamical system|discrete-time models]] with finite number of states and actions.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Jerzy |first1=Filar |author-link1= |title=Competitive Markov decision processes |last2=Vrieze |first2=Koos |publisher=Springer-Verlag |year=1997 |isbn=0-387-94805-8 |location=New York |pages=xii+393 |language=en}}</ref>
* ''Analytic Perturbation Theory and Its Applications'' (SIAM, 2013; co-authored with K.E. Avrachenkov and P.G. Howlett) presents a unified analysis of [[algebraic system]]s dependent on small perturbation parameters, applied to fields such as Markov processes and optimization.<ref name=":3">{{Cite book |last1=Avrachenkov |first1=Konstantin E. |url=http://epubs.siam.org/doi/book/10.1137/1.9781611973143 |title=Analytic Perturbation Theory and Its Applications |last2=Filar |first2=Jerzy A. |last3=Howlett |first3=Phil G. |date=2013-12-23 |publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics |isbn=978-1-61197-313-6 |location=Philadelphia, PA |language=en |doi=10.1137/1.9781611973143}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=O'Malley |first=Robert E. |date=2014 |title=Review of Analytic Perturbation Theory and Its Applications |url=http://www.jstor.org/stable/24248488 |journal=SIAM Review |volume=56 |issue=3 |pages=568–569 |jstor=24248488 |issn=0036-1445}}</ref>
* ''Hamiltonian Cycle Problem and Markov Chains'' (Springer, 2012; co-authored with [[Vivek Borkar|V.S. Borkar]], V. Ejov, and [[Giang Nguyen|G.T. Nguyen]]).<ref name=":4">{{Cite book |last1=Borkar |first1=Vivek S. |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-1-4614-3232-6 |title=Hamiltonian Cycle Problem and Markov Chains |last2=Ejov |first2=Vladimir |last3=Filar |first3=Jerzy A. |last4=Nguyen |first4=Giang T. |date=2012 |publisher=Springer New York |isbn=978-1-4614-3231-9 |series=International Series in Operations Research & Management Science |volume=171 |location=New York, NY |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-1-4614-3232-6}}</ref>
In game theory he introduced the concepts of switching controller stochastic game and games with incompetent players and explored a formulation of dynamic cooperative game.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Filar |first=J. A. |date=1981 |title=Ordered field property for stochastic games when the player who controls transitions changes from state to state |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF00935890 |journal=Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications |language=en |volume=34 |issue=4 |pages=503–515 |doi=10.1007/BF00935890 |issn=0022-3239|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Beck |first1=Justin D. |last2=Ejov |first2=Vladimir |last3=Filar |first3=Jerzy A. |date=2012 |title=Incompetence and impact of training in bimatrix games |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0005109812003019 |journal=Automatica |language=en |volume=48 |issue=10 |pages=2400–2408 |doi=10.1016/j.automatica.2012.06.046|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Filar |first1=Jerzy A. |last2=Petrosjan |first2=Leon A. |date=2000 |title=Dynamic Cooperative Games |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/S0219198900000044 |journal=International Game Theory Review |language=en |volume=02 |issue=1 |pages=47–65 |doi=10.1142/S0219198900000044 |issn=0219-1989|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In operations research he pioneered embeddings of the Hamiltonian cycle problem in Markov decision processes.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Filar |first1=Jerzy A. |last2=Krass |first2=Dmitry |date=1994 |title=Hamiltonian Cycles and Markov Chains |url=https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/moor.19.1.223 |journal=Mathematics of Operations Research |language=en |volume=19 |issue=1 |pages=223–237 |doi=10.1287/moor.19.1.223 |issn=0364-765X |archive-date=2022-11-13 |access-date=2025-03-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221113003028/http://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/moor.19.1.223 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":4" /> In environmental modeling he investigated uncertainty propagation and risk sensitivity to small changes in model parameters.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Zapert |first1=R. |last2=Gaertner |first2=P. S. |last3=Filar |first3=J. A. |date=1998-12-01 |title=Uncertainty propagation within an integrated model of climate change1 |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0140988398000140 |journal=Energy Economics |volume=20 |issue=5 |pages=571–598 |doi=10.1016/S0140-9883(98)00014-0 |bibcode=1998EneEc..20..571Z |issn=0140-9883|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Filar |first1=Jerzy A. |last2=Qiao |first2=Zhihao |last3=Streipert |first3=Sabrina |date=2020 |title=Risk sensitivity in Beverton–Holt fishery with multiplicative harvest |journal=Natural Resource Modeling |language=en |volume=33 |issue=3 |article-number=e12257 |doi=10.1111/nrm.12257 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2020NRM....33E2257F |issn=0890-8575}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Filar JA - Search Results - PubMed |url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=Filar+JA&cauthor_id=29484454 |access-date=2025-02-09 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Filar |first1=Jerzy A |last2=Krawczyk |first2=Jacek B |last3=Agrawal |first3=Manju R |date=2015-08-01 |title=Sustainability screw: role of relative production and abatement time scales |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1057/jors.2014.39 |journal=Journal of the Operational Research Society |volume=66 |issue=8 |pages=1259–1269 |doi=10.1057/jors.2014.39 |issn=0160-5682|url-access=subscription }}</ref> This linked to his more theoretical study of perturbation theory.<ref name=":3" />

In his final role as Director of the Centre for Applications in Resource Management (CARM), he worked on tools and simulations for evaluating the impacts of harvest policy changes.<ref name=":6" />

== Honours and awards ==
In 1985 he was awarded Environmental Science and Engineering Fellowship from the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]. In 2006, he was granted an Australian Research Council Professorial Fellowship (2006–2010).

His professional recognition include the 1981 Dr. Gurdas Chatterjee OPSEARCH Best Paper Award,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Filar |first=Jerzy |year=1982 |title=Dr. Gurdas Chatterjee Awards for 1980 and 1981 |journal=OPSearch. Journal of the Operational Research Society of India |volume=19 |pages=63–64}}</ref> the 2003 [[Fellow]] of the [[Australian Mathematical Society]], and the 2005 Ren Potts Medal from the Australian Society for Operations Research.<ref name="RenPottsAward">{{Cite web |title=ASOR Ren Potts Award |url=https://www.asor.org.au/index.php/award-medal/asor-ren-potts-award |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=www.asor.org.au}}</ref><ref name="JAFUNiSaNews">{{Cite web |date=2016-09-29 |title=Jerzy Filar honoured with award |url=https://unisa.edu.au/media-centre/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126101100/https://www.unisa.edu.au/media-centre/ |archive-date=2025-01-26 |access-date=2025-01-25 |website=University of South Australia |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2005-12-01 |title=Ren Potts Medal – the ASOR National Award. Ren Potts Medal 2005. Professor Jerzy Filar |url=https://asor.org.au/publication/files/dec2005/Ren.pdf |access-date=2025-03-15}}</ref> In 2007, he received the South Australian Science Excellence Award for Science Leadership and Management.<ref name="SASEA">{{Cite web |title=South Australian Science Excellence Award: Science Leadership and Management Category |url=http://www.scienceawards.sa.gov.au/vid-leadership1.html |access-date=2025-01-24 }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> In 2013, he was appointed to the Australian Research Council College of Experts.<ref name="JAFinARC">{{Cite web |title=ARC College of Experts |url=https://www.arc.gov.au/about/our-organisation/committees/arc-college-experts |access-date=2025-01-24}}</ref>

== Science fiction novelist ==
Since 2021, Filar has held the title of emeritus Professor of Applied Mathematics.  His academic career in the United States and Australia has informed his analysis of the interplay between technological advancements and the sustainability of Earth's life support systems. This led to the publication of his science fiction novel, ''YASMIN: The First Non-Artificial Intelligence Tool'', which incorporates mathematical concepts into its narrative.<ref name="JAF_YAS">{{Cite book |last=Filar |first=Jerzy A. |title=YASMIN: The First Non-Artificial Intelligence Tool |publisher=SORT PTY LTD |year=2023 |isbn=9780645980905 |edition=1st |location=Amazon |pages=291 |language=en |id={{ASIN|0645980900|country=de}}}}</ref>
